description: IRVEN is an energy analysis platform focused on identifying energy inefficiencies and helping businesses and institutions reduce costs through data-driven solutions. It uses energy consumption data, financial analysis, and public datasets from sources like NASA and CENACE to evaluate energy performance and identify opportunities for improvement.
summary:
IRVEN is a platform that helps cities and businesses make better energy decisions by combining NASA satellite and climate data with local infrastructure information.

We developed three interactive maps: a Government Map to identify areas affected by extreme heat and estimate cooling demand, an Industrial Map to compare potential locations for facilities, and a Diagnostic Map to evaluate buildings and estimate savings from improvements such as reflective roofs, added shade, and more efficient air conditioning.

IRVEN addresses the challenge by turning Earth observation data into practical information for planning and energy efficiency. This matters because extreme heat increases electricity demand and cooling costs. By helping users understand where energy is needed and where it could be saved, IRVEN supports better investments and more resilient communities.
details:
IRVEN helps governments and businesses understand how climate affects energy use and make better decisions about infrastructure, facility locations, and building improvements. It combines NASA satellite and climate data with local information in three interactive maps.

The Government Map helps users identify areas affected by extreme heat, explore estimated cooling demand, and prioritize infrastructure investments. The Industrial Map compares potential facility locations using temperature, humidity, solar radiation, and nearby infrastructure. The Diagnostic Map evaluates individual buildings and estimates potential savings from changes such as reflective roofs, additional shade, and more efficient air conditioning.

We developed the platform using JavaScript, TypeScript, React, and Next.js. MapLibre supports the interactive maps, while Google Earth Engine and custom processing scripts help analyze satellite data. Sources include NASA POWER, NASA MODIS, and NASA/USGS Landsat, alongside local information from organizations such as INEGI and CFE.

The creative part of IRVEN is connecting satellite observations to practical energy decisions. Users can move from identifying a hot urban area to comparing locations or exploring improvements for a specific building within the same platform.

Our intended impact is to help reduce unnecessary energy use, cooling costs, and pressure on electricity infrastructure. IRVEN supports preliminary assessments and helps users decide where more detailed studies and on-site measurements are needed.

Our team considered data availability, geographic resolution, local climate, infrastructure access, usability, and uncertainty. We distinguish measured data from modeled estimates because satellite observations alone cannot determine a building’s exact electricity consumption or guarantee savings.
